text:
sara: Heads-up — we're lining up a pen test for next month. Need input on RBAC temporary roles, KMS access window for evidence exports, and audit-log retention for the reviewers. Proposed main window: Wed Apr 7 22:00-02:00 UTC. Can we run a short dry-run Thu Apr 1 17:00-19:00 UTC? cc @julian @mike @olga

mike: +1 on planning. A few constraints: ephemeral RBAC should be max 8h, and we prefer scoped roles (no blanket admin). For KMS, we can create a decrypt-only ephemeral grant via the proxy, valid for the window. We should also produce an access manifest for auditors. :white_check_mark:

julian: For logs, what's the scope? App logs + infra audit + kube-audit? Need to know exact retention slice we should export. Also will we want raw logs or pre-filtered (to reduce noise)?

olga: From compliance side, we need full audit trail (kube-audit, API gateway, auth events) for the window + 72h buffer. For critical findings we require evidence snapshots and timeline. Proposed remediations SLA: P0/critical — 72h, P1 — 2 weeks. Is that acceptable?

mike: Sounds fair. We'll do: 1) dry-run export (Thu Apr 1) of 2 hours of synthetic traffic to validate pipeline, 2) main test Apr 7. For RBAC I'll draft a rolebinding template. Example rolebinding we plan to create for the testers:

```
# ephemeral rolebinding
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: pt-tester-binding
  namespace: production-readonly
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: pen-test-assessor@example.com
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: production-readonly-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

mike: Note: namespace = production-readonly (read + audit access). No write perms. We'll create an equivalent IAM policy for infra consoles.

julian: On KMS: plan is to generate an ephemeral CMK grant scoped to a single S3 prefix and timebox it. Evidence upload path suggestion: `s3://redwood-pt-evidence/2149005678/` with server-side encryption using the ephemeral grant. We'll snapshot logs and upload `evidence.zip`. Command for dry-run upload: `aws s3 cp evidence.zip s3://redwood-pt-evidence/2149005678/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <ephemeral-grant-id>`

deploy-bot: scheduled dry-run: Thu Apr 1 17:00 UTC — playbook 'pt-dryrun-2026' queued. Will post run artifacts to #eng-security when complete.

oncall: One operational ask: please provide a contact list (pager + slack) for the windows. We should have an on-call rotation for immediate triage if the testers trigger infra alarms.

olga: Compliance will require a signed evidence manifest and hash of artifacts. Please include a SHA256 manifest file alongside `evidence.zip` and note the KMS grant id used to encrypt each file.

mike: Agreed. I'll create a short checklist and a Jira epic (PT-4782) tonight. Checklist highlights:
- Create ephemeral RBAC roles and confirm with testers
- Provision KMS ephemeral grant and record grant id
- Create S3 prefix with restricted ACL and lifecycle (retain 90d then archive)
- Export logs (kube-audit, gateway, auth) to prefix and include SHA256 manifest
- Dry-run Thu Apr 1 — confirm artifacts and access
- Main window Apr 7 — monitor, collect artifacts, and open triage channel for findings

julian: One technical note: exporting kube-audit raw events at high QPS can spike storage/egress. For the dry-run we'll throttle to ~200 eps and verify the pipeline. If testers request higher fidelity during main window, we'll scope a dedicated export node.

olga: On retest policy — if we get a critical issue, retest window should be scheduled within 7 days of remediation deployment. Non-critical defers to the next monthly retest batch. We'll capture this in the remediation playbook.

mike: Perfect. Action items assigned: @julian — create S3 prefix & dry-run IAM/KMS grant by Fri Mar 27. @sara — confirm tester list and contact information by Mon Mar 24. @olga — draft compliance artifact checklist and remediation SLA text by Mon Mar 24. I'll schedule a 30m sync Mon Mar 24 16:00 UTC to finalize.

sara: Thanks — I'll confirm testers and contacts today. Also can you add a note in the dry-run to simulate a failed auth event so we can confirm alerting?

mike: Will do — add a small auth failure simulation in the dry-run. I'll update the Jira epic and post the checklist once ready. :thumbsup:
